title: Seller's Real Property Disclosure Statement
description: Hawaii Revised Statutes §508D-4 requires sellers of residential real property to deliver a written disclosure statement to the buyer before acceptance of the offer. The statement covers all material facts known to the seller, including structural, mechanical, environmental, and natural hazard conditions. Seller must update disclosure if conditions change before closing.

required_actions.note: Buyer may rescind within 15 calendar days of receipt. If disclosure is not provided, buyer may rescind any time before closing.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure
description: Hawaii Revised Statutes §467-14.5 requires licensees to disclose their agency relationship in writing at the earliest practicable time. Dual agency is permitted in Hawaii with informed written consent of both parties. The disclosure must identify whether the licensee represents the buyer, seller, or both.

required_actions.note: Disclosure required at earliest practicable time. Dual agency requires written informed consent from both parties.

title: Escrow Closing State
description: Hawaii is an escrow closing state. Closings are conducted through licensed escrow companies. Attorney presence is not required at closing. Title insurance is standard practice. Hawaii uses warranty deeds and the regular system of land registration alongside the Torrens (Land Court) system.

required_actions.note: Hawaii uses both regular system and Torrens (Land Court) system for property registration. Verify which system applies to the subject property.

title: Volcanic Lava Zone and Hazard Disclosure
description: Hawaii requires sellers to disclose whether the property is located within a volcanic lava flow hazard zone as mapped by the USGS. Hawaii County (Big Island) properties are classified in Lava Zones 1-9, with Zone 1 being highest risk. This is a required item on the statutory seller disclosure form under HRS §508D-15. Properties in high-risk zones may have difficulty obtaining insurance.

required_actions.note: Seller must disclose lava zone classification on the statutory disclosure form. USGS Lava Flow Hazard Zone maps determine classification.

metadata.note: Zones 1-2 are highest risk (active vents, recent flows). Affects insurance availability.

title: Leasehold Property Disclosure
description: Hawaii has a significant number of leasehold (vs. fee simple) residential properties, particularly on Oahu. HRS §508D-15 requires sellers to disclose whether the property is leasehold or fee simple, the lease expiration date, lease rent amounts, and any lease renegotiation terms. The Hawaii Land Reform Act (HRS §516) gives lessees certain conversion rights.

required_actions.note: Must disclose leasehold status, lease expiration date, current lease rent, escalation terms, and any conversion rights under HRS Chapter 516.

title: Special Management Area (SMA) and Shoreline Disclosure
description: Hawaii's Coastal Zone Management Act (HRS §205A) establishes Special Management Areas along all shorelines. Properties within the SMA are subject to additional permitting requirements for development or modifications. Sellers must disclose SMA status and any associated development restrictions.

required_actions.note: Disclose Special Management Area status. Improvements or modifications to SMA properties may require SMA Use Permits from the county.
